sources.title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces, Chapter 30: Condition Variables
sources.readScope: Complete extracted chapter text, all code listings, traces, references and homework questions (775 web-parsed lines; local extraction cross-check). Rendered PDF pages 13 and 14 inspected. Homework programs were not downloaded or executed; linked papers and other chapters were not read in this phase.
sources.application: Use explicit capacity and state at the asynchronous consumer boundary. Re-check current pending state when an active operation settles. Bound renderer draft admission and preserve only the latest complete pending snapshot.
sources.limits: The implementation is a JavaScript event-loop pipeline, not a pthread condition variable or native allocator. No mutex, spin loop, custom collector or memory-book-completion claim is derived from this chapter. Coalescing is valid here because each recovery write replaces a full snapshot, not because arbitrary queued work may be discarded.

sources.title: WHATWG HTML Standard, PageTransitionEvent.persisted
sources.readScope: Targeted persisted/pagehide/pageshow interface text only. The rest of the HTML Standard was not read.
sources.application: A pagehide notification can cache rather than destroy a document. Flush its newest snapshot, but reserve terminal disposal for explicit owner cleanup. A synthetic lifecycle regression covers continued saves; this is not browser back-forward-cache certification.
